subject: Upfront retainer, conditional credit slab & EU VAT entity routing
messages:
From: Alice Mercer <alice.mercer@acushield.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acushield Legal <legal@acushield.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 13:07:00 +0100
Subject: Payment cadence for pilot + VAT routing question

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the great demo last week — the team is excited to move the pilot to contract. Before procurement signs off we need to align on a couple of billing items:

1) Upfront retainer vs. prepayment: our procurement prefers a small upfront retainer (to be applied against first month) rather than a large prepayment.
2) Conditional credit slab: because the pilot will ramp, we'd like a conditional credit band that increases from GBP 50k to GBP 150k if we hit the agreed milestones.
3) VAT/entity routing: Acushield invoices from a UK HQ entity for EU Pilots; we need invoices that correctly route VAT to the UK entity (we can share the VAT reg cert).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: (a) issue an initial invoice for a 10% retainer (net30) and then follow a milestone-triggered invoice cadence, and (b) add a conditional credit increase tied to milestone acceptance? Also attaching the VAT cert and a proposed invoice cadence XLSX for your finance team.

Attachments: Acushield_TaxForm.pdf (pdf), Proposed_Invoice_Schedule.xlsx (xlsx)

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement hopes to close by end of month.

Best,
Alice Mercer
VP Finance, Acushield
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Mercer <alice.mercer@acushield.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment cadence for pilot + VAT routing question

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear summary and for the attachments. Short answers up front: yes on the retainer approach, and yes we can design a conditional credit slab tied to milestone acceptance. A few notes and a proposed path forward below.

Proposal (high level):
- Invoice 1 (retainer): 10% of the signed SOW, Net30.
- Milestone invoices: invoice on acceptance (Net30) for the milestone value; once milestone 2 is accepted we auto-increase the credit band to the agreed higher threshold.
- Credit slab mechanics: initial credit cap GBP 50k; milestone-driven increase to GBP 150k; Redwood will require a 14-day cure period on overdue invoices before suspending trial access.
- VAT/entity routing: we can route invoices to your UK entity and include VAT registration details you provided. Our billing system requires the billed-entity name and VAT ID in the contract metadata before we issue the first invoice.

Required next steps from Acushield:
1) Confirm billed entity name + VAT ID (we have the cert but need the exact legal name to put on invoices).
2) Confirm milestone acceptance definition for each tranche (one-sentence acceptance criteria is sufficient).
3) Sign the SOW with the retainer and milestone schedule attached.

Internal ask: Priyom / Vivek — can you review the proposed 14-day cure period and the conditional credit increase flow? If acceptable, I’ll get legal to add the specific milestone-trigger wording into the SOW and loop procurement.

Warm regards,
Rachel Kim
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment cadence for pilot + VAT routing question

Rachel — quick notes from finance perspective:

- 14-day cure looks fine for a pilot; for larger accounts we normally go 7-10 days but given this is milestone-driven and the retainer is small, 14 days is acceptable.
- Operationally we need the exact entity string to map the VAT ID in our billing engine; recommend we require Acushield to provide a completed W-8/W-9 equivalent (for EU, an invoicing contact + VAT cert is enough).
- Credit slab: require a simple rollback clause — if milestone acceptance is disputed beyond 30 days we revert to initial GBP 50k cap until dispute is resolved. Adds protection vs. open-ended credit.

I’ll draft the credit-slab mechanics for the SOW. Vivek — are there any caveats from a collections/SLA standpoint?

Thanks,
Priyom
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment cadence for pilot + VAT routing question

+1 to Priyom's rollback suggestion. A couple operational points to include in the SOW and billing notes:

- Auto-escalation path: if invoice is 7 days overdue, automated reminder; at 14 days we hit the manual collections queue and notify the account team; at 21 days access is suspended until payment or agreed plan.
- For the conditional credit increase we will: (a) require signed milestone acceptance email (one-line confirmation accepted), (b) system flag to raise cap (manual ops step to mitigate fraud), (c) 30-day trial window to confirm usage patterns — if usage exceeds the increased cap before milestone acceptance, finance will invoice overage.
- VAT handling: once we have the exact billed-entity string and VAT ID we will issue the initial retainer invoice to the UK entity and mark VAT appropriately; please ask Acushield to copy legal@acushield.com on that confirmation so legal has the paper trail.

Rachel — once Priyom shares the drafted mechanics I can sign off and we can send the SOW to Acushield with a one-page appendix summarizing billing flow.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Manager, Customer Finance
Redwood Inference
